skill.description: Choose suitable CLI, API, browser, Qt, or Windows desktop testing methods based on observed capabilities and acceptance requirements.

security_audit.summary: All 101 static findings are false positives in context: documented local automation, public research citations, ordinary identifiers, readable multilingual documentation, and compact test reports. The worker uses argument arrays, validates target identity, rejects ambiguous selectors, and limits execution time. No evidence found of credential theft, unauthorized network transmission, prompt injection, or concealed executable payloads.

content.value_statement: Choosing a test interface can waste effort or leave acceptance requirements unverified. This skill guides interface discovery and provides scoped Windows automation with durable progress evidence.
actual_capabilities: Select CLI, API, DOM, Windows UIA, Qt, or visual checks according to acceptance requirements and observed interfaces.
Probe verified launcher descendants to identify actual window owners and report ambiguous ownership.
Inspect target-window controls, supported UIA patterns, and bounded tree depths without reading input values by default.
Execute UIA set, invoke, and wait steps with exact selectors, ancestor scopes, and per-step window selection.
Apply a worker-level timeout and recover completed steps and uncertain actions from durable progress journals.
Guide business-result assertions, fresh output verification, Playwright interactions, Qt signal tests, and controlled visual comparisons.
limitations: The UIA driver requires Windows, PowerShell 7, Python 3.10 or later, and an interactive desktop with accessible controls.
The driver supports only set, invoke, and wait; it does not implement global keyboard input, dragging, or coordinate clicking.
The installed package excludes development tests and fixtures; documented reproduction commands require the maintenance repository and its test dependencies.
Historical sample results do not establish universal compatibility or speed gains; several platforms and Electron workflows remain unverified.

use_cases.title: Test a Desktop Executable Without Source
use_cases.description: Identify the correct process, inspect available UIA patterns, and verify an export through actual controls and a fresh output file.

use_cases.title: Verify an Asynchronous Web Form
use_cases.description: Choose scoped DOM automation and connect a real button event to its request, business response, visible state, and output.

use_cases.title: Separate Qt Logic and Release Acceptance
use_cases.description: Use pytest-qt for signals and cancellation, then identify additional checks needed for the delivered executable and its appearance.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Testing Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [application] and [acceptance requirement]. Identify available test interfaces, recommend one route, and state the evidence needed to prove success.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: select an interface before building tests.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Windows Target
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [PID] and [executable path] without changing application state. Identify window ownership, useful UIA patterns, selector ambiguity, and any unavailable capabilities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: discover controls in a source-free desktop application.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Web Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the export button at [test URL] using the existing browser framework. Verify the real click, business response, completion state, and fresh artifact contents.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: validate a complete browser workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Recoverable Desktop Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a UIA plan for [workflow] using observed selectors and scoped windows. Add condition waits, a hard deadline, and progress evidence. Define postconditions and timeout recovery without blindly repeating mutations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: automate stateful desktop acceptance checks.

output_examples.input: Choose a test approach for a Windows executable that exports a file.
output: Route: inspect the verified process and use UIA if the required Value and Invoke patterns are available.
Evidence: observe completion, then reopen a newly generated output and check its expected contents.
Boundary: a returned Invoke call alone does not prove the export succeeded.

output_examples.input: Interpret a hard timeout after a desktop action started.
output: Status: the automation worker stopped; the target application remains running.
Recovery: retain completed journal steps and mark the interrupted action outcome as unknown.
Next check: inspect application state and output before deciding whether another action is safe.

output_examples.input: Determine whether Qt signal tests prove that the packaged application works.
output: Internal coverage: Qt signal and cancellation tests can verify event-loop behavior.
Remaining coverage: launch the delivered executable and verify required user flows and actual outputs.
Visual boundary: offscreen or property checks do not prove correct rendering.

best_practices: Start with the acceptance requirement and a small capability probe before selecting or installing a framework.
Use unique scoped selectors, fresh test data, observable postconditions, and bounded execution.
Review durable progress and actual outputs after interruption; preserve uncertain outcomes and report uncovered requirements.
anti_patterns: Treating HTTP success, an emitted signal, or a returned UIA call as proof of the complete user workflow.
Hiding selector ambiguity with the first match or assuming every application exposes the same automation patterns.
Blindly replaying a timed-out mutation or reporting unavailable and skipped checks as passed.

faq.question: Does this skill always avoid screenshots?
faq.answer: No. Visual requirements still need controlled image evidence. Structured interfaces are preferred only when they can prove the required behavior.

faq.question: Can it test a Windows application without source code?
faq.answer: Yes, when the target exposes suitable UIA controls and patterns. The driver requires an explicit process identity and an accessible interactive desktop.

faq.question: Which desktop actions are implemented?
faq.answer: The helper implements ValuePattern set, InvokePattern invoke, and conditional waits on name, value, or enabled properties.

faq.question: What happens when the hard timeout expires?
faq.answer: The wrapper stops its PowerShell worker, preserves the application, and recovers journal evidence. Started actions can remain uncertain and must not be blindly repeated.

faq.question: Are browser and Qt test suites included?
faq.answer: No. The package provides guidance and historical evidence. Development tests and fixtures require the separate maintenance repository and prepared dependencies.

faq.question: Does it guarantee faster testing or broad platform support?
faq.answer: No. Historical results cover specific samples. They do not establish universal speed gains or verified support for every browser, desktop platform, or framework.
